newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka police avoid clash over religious statue.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka police avoid clash over religious statue.

text.p: Residents of a small Sri Lankan town burnt tyres and threatened more violence if police failed to replace a statue of St. Anthony that was torn down earlier by a court order, police said on Friday.

People of Weliweriya, about 16 km (10 miles) northeast of Colombo, threw stones at police vehicles, blocked roads and demanded local authorities give them back the statue that was taken down for obstructing a public place, they said.

"We took the statue down on Wednesday night in accordance with a court ruling. It was the village council that went to court asking for its removal," a senior police officer in charge of the town's security told Reuters.
The statue, placed in the town's congested marketplace and bus stand area, was ordered removed because it obstructed pedestrians and vehicle traffic, he said.
But the town's Catholics came out in force the next morning, he said, accusing police and council members of religious inequality.
Nearly 70 percent of Sri Lanka's 18 million population are Buddhist. Christians make up about eight percent while the balance consist of Hindus and Moslems.
"We didn't want this to blow up into a major religious issue, so we allowed the people to put up another statue in the same place till we arrive at a negotiated settlement later," the officer said.
He did not say what the settlement might be, but confirmed that the demonstrators had gone home peacefully.
